headline: High: shared file/MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; no direct sandbox evidence reduces confidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can consume artifacts via workflows and APIs, while agent B processes PDFs/text/images and uses MCP plus natural-language commands. A shared workspace or file handoff is plausible, so B could ingest A-produced content as instructions. This is inferred from docs-only profiles, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent A writes content that agent B later opens from a shared file or MCP channel
IF agent B parses A-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
Add a provenance banner to A-generated files
Require B to treat file contents as untrusted data
Restrict B MCP tools to allowlisted sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has allowlisted network egress and handles artifacts/parameters; agent B has broad egress, uses multiple hosted AI backends, and handles API keys plus document files. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts or documents can flow from A into B and then to third-party APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this remains medium, not high.
conditions: IF A artifacts or parameters are placed in a workspace that B can read
IF B sends opened documents or prompts to hosted model APIs
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Block B from uploading sensitive files to hosted APIs
Store API keys outside shared directories
Redact parameters before B reads them
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can call REST/gRPC APIs and B can use MCP plus multiple model backends; both also have network egress. That creates overlapping mutable external actions if they target the same service or document set, even though the profiles do not show filesystem write or git access. Because the conflict surface is plausible but not explicit, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same external API resource
IF B uses MCP tools against resources that A also updates
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Disable concurrent edits to shared targets
Log and reject conflicting updates
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces workflow artifacts and parameters, and B is a natural-language document-processing agent that can render or act on inputs from files and MCP. That makes it likely B will treat A outputs as authoritative unless explicitly verified. Because downstream actions can propagate incorrect facts into generated diagrams or API calls, the blast radius is broad and defaults appear unsafe.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated artifacts as source material without verification
IF B uses those artifacts to produce diagrams or API-backed outputs
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A outputs
Mark A outputs as untrusted input in B
Add checksum or schema validation between agents
Limit B to read-only rendering for A artifacts
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: A touches artifacts and parameters with allowlisted egress, while B handles PDFs, images, and API keys and can send content to multiple third-party model providers. The pair therefore creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch and secret-handling exposure path, but the profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so the compliance risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are placed into B for processing
IF B forwards those materials to hosted model providers with different retention policies
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Use local-only models for sensitive documents
Separate secret-bearing inputs from diagram inputs
Document retention settings for each backend
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
